book_title: Uyun al-Akhbar wa Funun al-Athar, Volume One: The Life of the Prophet

preface.title: A Yemeni Historian and His Prophet

chapters.title: Why This History Needed Writing
chapters.rationale: The book's own foreword, its argument that the community required designated successors, and the author's stated plan form one opening statement of intent.

chapters.title: The Pure Line: Ishmael to Adnan
chapters.rationale: The claim that the Prophet's forefathers were free of idolatry, traced through Ishmael and the Arab tribes of the Hijaz down to Quraysh and its tongue.

chapters.title: Qusayy Takes Mecca
chapters.rationale: The rise of Qusayy — his exile, return, war with Khuza'ah, purchase of the Ka'bah key, and seizure of the city's offices.

chapters.title: Abd Manaf and the Breaker of Bread
chapters.rationale: The inheritance passes from Qusayy to 'Abd Manaf and then to Hashim, whose feeding of pilgrims and Ilaf trade pacts made the family's name.

chapters.title: Shaybah al-Hamd: The Boy Brought Back from Yathrib
chapters.rationale: The birth, recovery, and naming of 'Abd al-Muttalib, with the elegies and praise poems that fixed his reputation.

chapters.title: The Elephant and the Well
chapters.rationale: Abraha's failed march on the Ka'bah and 'Abd al-Muttalib's excavation of Zamzam — two proofs of the Sacred House's protection and its guardian's standing.

chapters.title: The Vow and the Hundred Camels
chapters.rationale: 'Abd al-Muttalib's vow to sacrifice a tenth son, the casting of lots that ransomed 'Abdullah, and the priestess who saw the light in his face.

chapters.title: A Light Born in the Year of the Elephant
chapters.rationale: 'Abdullah's death, Amina's vision, the Prophet's birth, his nursing among Banu Sa'd, and the splitting of his breast.

chapters.title: The Orphan and His Grandfather
chapters.rationale: Amina's death, 'Abd al-Muttalib's tenderness toward the boy and his bequest of him to Abu Talib, with the elegies that followed his own death.

chapters.title: Bahira Sees the Sign
chapters.rationale: Abu Talib's guardianship, the journey to Busra and the monk's warning, and the boy's standing in his uncle's household.

chapters.title: Born in the Ka'bah, Raised Beside Him
chapters.rationale: Fatima bint Asad's vision and 'Ali's birth inside the Ka'bah, followed by the rebuilding of the Ka'bah and the War of the Ungodly.

chapters.title: Khadijah Proposes
chapters.rationale: The marriage contract with Khadijah, her children, and Waraqah's confirmation that the awaited prophet had come.

chapters.title: Tuesday: The First to Believe
chapters.rationale: 'Ali's upbringing in the Prophet's house, his conversion the day after Khadijah's, the defence of a child's faith, and the gathering of the clan.

chapters.title: By God, I Will Not Abandon You
chapters.rationale: The open call, Quraysh's successive delegations to Abu Talib, and his refusal — culminating in his verses of protection.

chapters.title: The Long Poem of the Protector
chapters.rationale: Abu Talib's praise of his people, al-Walid's verdict on the Qur'an, and the great Lamiyyah with the author's assessment of Abu Talib's concealed faith.

chapters.title: The Tree That Came When Called
chapters.rationale: Abu Qays's warning poem, the Quraysh's verbal assault, 'Ali's sermon on the miracle of the tree, and Abu Jahl's failed stoning.

chapters.title: Crossing the Sea to the Negus
chapters.rationale: The migration to Abyssinia, Abu Talib's letter, Ja'far's testimony before the Negus, and the king's protection of the emigrants.

chapters.title: Hamza, Umar, and the Parchment in the Ka'bah
chapters.rationale: Two powerful conversions, then the Quraysh's written boycott of Banu Hashim and the poetry it provoked.

chapters.title: The Document Eaten Away
chapters.rationale: Umm Jamil's abuse, Abu Talib's appeals to Abu Lahab, the protection of Abu Salamah, and the tearing of the parchment that ends the siege.

chapters.title: The Night Journey and the Fifty Prayers
chapters.rationale: The journey to Jerusalem and the heavens, the origin of the call to prayer, the reduction of the prayers, and the trial the vision became for Mecca.

chapters.title: The Year of Sorrow
chapters.rationale: The Prophet's endurance, then the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah within a single year and the Quraysh's new boldness against him.

chapters.title: Ta'if, Addas, and the Tribes
chapters.rationale: The rejection at Ta'if, the Christian slave who kissed his feet, and the presentation of Islam to the Arab tribes at the pilgrimage seasons.

chapters.title: The Pledges at al-Aqabah
chapters.rationale: The first Khazraj converts, the two pledges at al-'Aqabah, Mus'ab's teaching mission, and the naming of the twelve chieftains.

chapters.title: The Bed and the Cave
chapters.rationale: The plot at Dar al-Nadwa, 'Ali's night on the Prophet's bed, and the flight to the cave with the author's argument about who truly ransomed the Prophet.

chapters.title: Building the Mosque, Closing the Doors
chapters.rationale: The camel that chose the site, the raising of the mosque, and the command that every door onto it be shut except 'Ali's.

chapters.title: Sermons, Brotherhood, and the New Community
chapters.rationale: The first Friday sermons, the pact of brotherhood, Salman's conversion, and the emergence of the hypocrites within the new city.

chapters.title: First Raids and the Sacred Month
chapters.rationale: Hamza's banner at al-'Ais through the raids of Buwat, al-'Ushayrah and Nakhlah, ending with the killing of Ibn al-Hadrami during a sacred month.

chapters.title: The Caravan and the Dream of Atikah
chapters.rationale: Abu Sufyan's caravan, 'Atikah's warning vision, the mobilization of Quraysh, and the two armies converging on the wells of Badr.

chapters.title: The Day the Angels Fought
chapters.rationale: The single combats, the rout of the polytheists, and the full roll of those slain and martyred at Badr.

chapters.title: Ransom, Grief, and Triumph in Verse
chapters.rationale: The killing of the captives al-Nadr and 'Uqbah, al-'Abbas's ransom, the news reaching Mecca, and the long cycle of victory poetry.

chapters.title: Reprisals: Suwaiq, Qaynuqa, and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf
chapters.rationale: Abu Sufyan's revenge raid, the expulsion of Banu Qaynuqa', and the assassination of the poet Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

chapters.title: Fatimah's Wedding
chapters.rationale: The companions' proposal, Gabriel's confirmation, the armour sold for a dowry, and the wedding feast that fed sixteen hundred.

chapters.title: Uhud: The Archers Who Left the Hill
chapters.rationale: The Quraysh mobilization, the Prophet's vision, the early Muslim advance, and the abandonment of the archers' position that turned victory into rout.

chapters.title: The Lion of God and the Liver of Hind
chapters.rationale: 'Ali's defence of the wounded Prophet, the killing and mutilation of Hamza, the burial of the martyrs, and Hind's boasting verses.

chapters.title: Hamra al-Asad and the Roll of the Fallen
chapters.rationale: The pursuit to Hamra' al-Asad, the naming of the slain on both sides, and the great body of elegy composed for the day of Uhud.

chapters.title: Betrayal at al-Raji and Bir Ma'unah
chapters.rationale: The two treacheries in which small parties of instructors sent to distant tribes were killed, with the poetry mourning them.

chapters.title: Expelling Banu al-Nadir
chapters.rationale: The plot to drop a rock on the Prophet, the siege of Banu al-Nadir, their departure for Khaybar, and the verses commemorating it.

chapters.title: Dhat al-Riqa, Badr al-Akhirah, and a Mother Buried
chapters.rationale: The prayer of fear, the man who seized the Prophet's sword, the unmet appointment at Badr, and the death of Fatima bint Asad.

chapters.title: Digging the Trench
chapters.rationale: The Jewish embassies to Quraysh and Ghatafan, the digging of the trench with its miracles, the siege, and Banu Qurayza's breach of covenant.

chapters.title: Amr ibn Abd Wudd Crosses the Ditch
chapters.rationale: 'Ali's duel with the champion 'Amr, the collapse of confederate morale, Na'im's stratagem, and the wind that scattered the armies.

chapters.title: Judgment on Banu Qurayza
chapters.rationale: The siege of Banu Qurayza, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's ruling, the executions in the market, and the poetry composed on the trench and its aftermath.

chapters.title: Banu Lahyan, Dhu Qarad, and al-Muraysi
chapters.rationale: Three expeditions of pursuit and reprisal, ending with the defeat of Banu al-Mustaliq and the marriage to Juwayriyah.

chapters.title: A Quarrel at the Watering Place
chapters.rationale: The clash between Muhajirun and Ansar, Ibn Ubayy's threat, the slander affair, and the hadith likening 'Ali to the Messiah.

chapters.title: The Treaty at Hudaybiyah
chapters.rationale: The pilgrimage turned back, the Pledge of al-Ridwan, the erasure of the Prophet's title from the document, and the terms that dismayed the Muslims.

chapters.title: The Gate of Khaybar
chapters.rationale: The march north, the banner given to 'Ali, the killing of Marhab and the tearing out of the fortress gate, followed by the terms and the poisoned sheep.

chapters.title: Khaybar's Echo and the Compensatory Umrah
chapters.rationale: The false rumour spread in Mecca, the poetry on Khaybar, Ja'far's return from Abyssinia, and the 'Umrah of the Qada'.

chapters.title: Three Commanders at Mu'tah
chapters.rationale: The expedition to the Byzantine frontier in which Ja'far, Zayd, and Ibn Rawahah fell in succession, with the elegies for the slain.

chapters.title: Khuza'ah Calls for Help
chapters.rationale: The attack on Khuza'ah that voided the truce, Abu Sufyan's failed mission to Medina, and the preparations for the march on Mecca.

chapters.title: On the Road to Mecca
chapters.rationale: The rulings on fasting and shortening prayer while travelling, the conversions of Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, and the army's approach to Marr al-Zahran.

chapters.title: Whoever Enters His House Is Safe
chapters.rationale: Abu Sufyan's submission, the entry of the armies, the transfer of the banner from Sa'd to 'Ali, and the handful of men marked for death.

chapters.title: Breaking the Idols
chapters.rationale: The key restored to 'Uthman ibn Talha, the sermon at the Ka'bah door, Khalid's excess at Banu Judhimah, and the destruction of the idols.

chapters.title: Ambush in the Valley of Hunayn
chapters.rationale: Hawazin's massed forces, Durayd's rejected counsel, the Muslim flight, and the handful who held their ground around the Prophet.

chapters.title: Awtas, Ta'if, and the Siege That Failed
chapters.rationale: The pursuit to Awtas, the killing of Durayd, the poetry on Hunayn, and the unsuccessful siege of Ta'if with its catapults and withdrawal.

chapters.title: Camels for the Newly Reconciled
chapters.rationale: The return of Hawazin's captives, the gifts to those whose hearts were to be won, and the Prophet's consolation of the aggrieved Ansar.

chapters.title: Tabuk and the Men Left Behind
chapters.rationale: Ka'b ibn Zuhayr's pardon, the expedition to Tabuk with 'Ali left over Medina, the treaties with Ayla and Ukaydir, and the three who stayed behind.

chapters.title: The Year of Delegations
chapters.rationale: Surat Bara'ah entrusted to 'Ali, and the succession of tribal delegations from Thaqif, Tamim, Tayy, Kindah, Himyar and beyond.

chapters.title: Letters, Taxes, and Instructions to Yemen
chapters.rationale: The Prophet's letters to the kings of Himyar and to 'Amr ibn Hazm setting out zakat, jizyah, and the rites, with the author's comparison to Ahl al-Bayt narrations.

chapters.title: The Smaller Expeditions
chapters.rationale: The catalogue of detachments — Ghalib, Zayd, 'Abdullah ibn Anis, 'Amr ibn al-'As and others — sent out on missions of raid and assassination.

chapters.title: Dispatches, Assassins, and Yemen
chapters.rationale: The killings of Abu 'Afak and Asma' bint Marwan, the affair of Thumamah, and 'Ali's twin missions to Najran and Yemen with the disputes they caused.

chapters.title: Rites of the Farewell Pilgrimage
chapters.rationale: The Prophet's last pilgrimage and the rulings on ihram, sacrifice, the miqats, talbiyah, and the circumambulation drawn from it.

chapters.title: Arafah and the Sermon of Farewell
chapters.rationale: The standing at 'Arafah, the sermon abolishing usury and blood feuds, the departure to Muzdalifah and Mina, and the stoning and shaving.

chapters.title: Ghadir Khumm
chapters.rationale: The declaration at Ghadir Khumm and the verses said to accompany it — the book's central argument for 'Ali's succession.

chapters.title: The Case for the Guardian
chapters.rationale: The accumulated virtues — the closed doors, the mubahala, Bara'ah, the rank of Aaron — marshalled as evidence for 'Ali's imamate.

chapters.title: The Illness and the Undelivered Document
chapters.rationale: The envy of the hypocrites, the dispatch of Usama's army, the onset of the fatal illness, and the dispute over Abu Bakr leading the prayer.

chapters.title: Washing, Shrouding, and the Empty Place
chapters.rationale: The refusal to let him write his final instruction, his last words, the washing and burial by 'Ali, and the elegies of Hassan ibn Thabit.
